author: NorthEast News Desk
body: New Hampshire’s state primary concluded without significant incidents, according to the state Department of Justice, after election-law personnel monitored voting across hundreds of polling places.

The department said 39 inspectors from its Election Law Unit visited about 260 polling locations. Their work included observing procedures and assisting local officials when questions arose. The department coordinated with the Secretary of State’s office during the voting period.

A dedicated hotline staffed by four attorneys, two investigators and a paralegal received 83 contacts. The state did not identify any of those calls as producing a significant election problem. Secretary of State David Scanlan said he had no concerns about disruption and noted that state personnel routinely monitor elections and help local administrators.

Federal election monitors were also assigned to Manchester and Nashua. New Hampshire was one of six states receiving federal monitors for the primary. The state’s report provides an initial operational assessment rather than a certification of every result; official canvassing and other post-election procedures continue under the normal schedule.
dek: State inspectors visited roughly 260 polling places, while an election-law hotline handled 83 contacts without a significant incident.
headline: New Hampshire election monitors report smooth state primary
